label: TP
reason: Both alerts are true positives. Alert 1 (java/xss) has user input flowing directly to the HTML sink at lines 59-62 via concatenation; although encodeForHTML is called, the taint reaches the sink expression before or during encoding, making the resolved sink value dependent on attacker input. Alert 2 (java/sql-injection) has user input flowing directly to the SQL query construction at line 56; the doSomething function attempts to sanitize by removing the first element and taking the second, but the logic incorrectly selects index 1 (which holds the original user input 'param') instead of index 0 ('safe'), so the resolved sink value remains attacker-controlled.

evidence.note: XSS sink where encoded SQL is printed; taint reaches here despite encoding attempt.
SQL injection sink where user input is concatenated into query; doSomething returns user input due to incorrect array indexing.
